Spoken word
Before the ships, before the trade,
Verse 1
Along the great river, the rice was made.
Three thousand years, our own to claim,
Oryza glaberrima, that's its name.
Our ancestors grew it, our ancestors knew,
A rice of Africa, strong and true.
Red in the husk, or black some say,
Verse 2
A different rice than the world knows today.
It stood through drought, it stood through flood,
It stood through iron-heavy mud.
Weeds could not choke it, pests could not win,
Africa's rice, so tough within.
African rice, rise again,
Chorus
Grown by our fathers, grown by our men!
Red and rich, and full of pride,
Don't let this heritage fade and hide!
We are Acres, hear us say,
African rice belongs today!
Cook your jollof, cook it right,
Verse 3
With the rice that came before the light.
Cook your waakye, beans and grain,
Bring back the rice from which it came.
Before the pot was ever red,
African rice was already fed.
Then came the rice from across the sea,
Verse 4
Higher yield, so it seemed to be.
Slowly our own was pushed aside,
Forgotten in fields where it used to thrive.
But red rice still carries what white rice lacks,
More of the good things, deep in its tracks.
African rice, rise again,
Chorus
Grown by our fathers, grown by our men!
Red and rich, and full of pride,
Don't let this heritage fade and hide!
We are Acres, hear us say,
African rice belongs today!
Ghana and Togo, the hills still hold
Bridge
Pockets of red rice, a story untold.
Find the farmers who still know the way,
Learn how they grow it, learn how they stay.
This rice fed our people for generations long,
Now let it feed us, now sing the song.
African rice, rise again,
Final chorus
Grown by our fathers, grown by our men!
Red and rich, and full of pride,
Don't let this heritage fade and hide!
We are Acres, hear us say,
African rice belongs today!
Ask for it. Grow it. Cook it. Remember it.
